main_issue: Who should pay for juices/soft drinks for the housewarming after the shared drinks fund was spent on alcohol

A-B.evidence: B initially proposes everyone chip in (T4), later accepts A already contributed and excludes him (T14); A only protests paying again (T13) and asks for a plan (T7).

A-C.evidence: C concedes A is covered because of his extra money (T17), which fits A's objection (T13); C's earlier complaint blamed the spending (T5), but the end arrangement exempts A.

A-D.evidence: D objected to all money going on alcohol (T6) and A admitted the mistake (T7); D endorses C's plan (T12), which exempts A, though A never states agreement.

B-C.evidence: C rejects B's proposals (T5, T9, T11, T15); B asks C for a solution (T16); C proposes drinkers split the bill (T17), partly like B's T14 but excluding D; B hasn't accepted.

B-D.evidence: B proposed that he and D buy juices and split cost (T8); D then backed C's drinkers-pay idea (T12), diverging from B's plan; D is on B's side on non-alcoholic options.

C-D.evidence: D: 'He's got a point' (T6) and 'That sounds fair' (T12); C defends D by saying she doesn't drink and shouldn't pay (T15), then proposes drinkers split (T17).
